categories.description: COBOL compilation unit identified by PROGRAM-ID; batch/online role needs invocation evidence.
required_evidence: Compiler dialect and options; complete source and COPY/REPLACE closure
Procedure entry, file/Db2/CICS calls, return codes and all branches

categories.description: Reusable COBOL declarations or source fragments; COPY can insert executable source as well as layouts.
required_evidence: Each including program and replacement parameters
Full declaration/layout including REDEFINES, OCCURS, level 88 and encoding

categories.description: JCL job stream; an inventory of steps is not its full execution semantics.
required_evidence: JOB, EXEC, DD, PROC/INCLUDE and symbol expansion
Step order, conditional skips, return codes, dataset lifecycle and restart

categories.description: Cataloged/in-stream procedure; resolve call-site overrides before explaining execution.
required_evidence: All procedure invocations and nested procedure dependencies
Symbol values and EXEC/DD overrides

categories.description: JCL include or partial stream; cannot be treated as a complete job.
required_evidence: Containing jobs and exact insertion location
Missing JOB/PROC context and substitution values

categories.description: CICS BMS physical map macros; screen behavior also resides in transactions and programs.
required_evidence: Mapset/map/field definitions plus symbolic map copybooks
CICS transaction-to-program bindings, SEND/RECEIVE behavior, validation and navigation

categories.description: SQL/DDL statements or Db2 definitions; source presence does not prove runtime database semantics.
required_evidence: Db2 subsystem/version, current schema, bind/package options and authorization
Tables/views/keys/types/NULLs/triggers/procedures and transaction boundaries

categories.description: Db2 table descriptor / host-variable declaration; not a business program by itself.
required_evidence: Base table DDL and generated host-variable structure
Nullable indicator variables and CCSID/type conversion rules

categories.description: Control statements consumed by a specific utility, not standalone executable source.
required_evidence: Invoking utility and exact product/version/options
DD bindings, control members, exits, record layouts and installation defaults

categories.description: REXX script; host commands and ADDRESS environments can perform external work.
required_evidence: TSO/ISPF/USS/host environment and invoked routines
Host command side effects, return codes and datasets
Invoking TSO context and positional/keyword parameters
Nested CLISTs, commands, allocation and error handling

categories.description: PL/I source unit; requires its own language adapter.
required_evidence: Compiler dialect/options and include dependencies
Data representation, condition handling and external interfaces

categories.description: Assembler source or macros; requires machine and macro semantics.
required_evidence: Architecture, macro libraries and linkage conventions
Data representation, registers, system services and side effects

categories.description: CICS resource definitions, including transaction/program/file/map bindings.
required_evidence: CSD export/version and resource group/list membership
Transactions, programs, security, file modes and startup overrides

categories.description: Scheduler commands or definitions; product/version and application conventions must be resolved.
required_evidence: CA7 or other product/version, calendars, predecessors, event conditions
Business dates, restart/rerun, late handling and external schedules

categories.description: No reliable structural match; do not silently discard or infer conversion from the filename.
required_evidence: Source type/export encoding and owner
How the member is invoked or consumed and complete dependencies

categories.description: Conflicting content signatures or filename/content mismatch; automated translation is blocked.
required_evidence: Resolve the actual content type and authoritative source member
Explain mixed exports or naming mistakes before retrying as a new process

utilities.name: ICEMAN
utilities.behavior: Sorts, merges, selects, joins, reformats and splits records according to control statements. SORT is a site-resolved alias: confirm that the installed product is IBM DFSORT.
required_evidence: Product/version and installation defaults; SORTIN/SORTOUT/SORTWK DDs
SYSIN/SORTCNTL/INCLUDE/OMIT/INREC/OUTREC/OUTFIL/JOINKEYS statements and symbols
Record formats, offsets/types, E15/E35 exits and tie-breaking requirements
risks: EBCDIC collation, packed/zoned decimals and duplicate ordering differ from ordinary Python sorting
Filtering or reformatting can encode business rules; do not reduce the step to a generic sort
Alternative sort vendors and exits can alter behavior

utilities.name: ICETOOL
utilities.behavior: Runs dataset analysis, selection, reporting and multiple DFSORT operations within one step.
required_evidence: TOOLIN, TOOLMSG, DFSMSG and all referenced xxxCNTL members
All operator inputs/outputs, counts and return-code requirements
risks: A single step can contain multiple dependent operations and reports
Exact operators, options and record types require dedicated tests

utilities.name: IDCAMS
utilities.behavior: Processes catalog/access-method commands such as DEFINE, DELETE, LISTCAT and REPRO; actual effects depend on the complete command stream.
required_evidence: SYSIN commands, IF/THEN conditions and SET MAXCC/LASTCC changes
VSAM organization, key length/offset, alternate indexes, catalog aliases and dataset attributes
Input/output DD bindings and reset/reuse behavior
risks: REPRO is not always equivalent to copying a flat text file
DELETE/DEFINE can change persistent catalog state; read-only discovery must never execute these commands
Return-code rewriting and error tolerance can be business-significant

utilities.name: IEFBR14
utilities.behavior: The program returns zero, but surrounding JCL invokes allocation and disposition processing that can create or delete datasets.
required_evidence: Every DD and DISP normal/abnormal disposition
Dataset allocation attributes and downstream dependencies
risks: Dropping a no-op program may drop required JCL side effects
A zero program return code does not prove dataset creation, deletion or initialization parity

utilities.name: IEBGENER
utilities.behavior: Copies/generates records and can edit data or change record layout using control statements.
required_evidence: SYSUT1/SYSUT2/SYSIN/SYSPRINT and all GENERATE/RECORD/MEMBER statements
Concatenation order, record lengths, encoding and output allocation
risks: Not every invocation is a byte-for-byte copy
Truncation, padding, generated records and member output need explicit behavior

utilities.name: ICEGENER
utilities.behavior: DFSORT facility for qualifying IEBGENER operations; execution can use the DFSORT copy function or transfer to IEBGENER.
required_evidence: All IEBGENER evidence plus installed ICEGENER defaults and fallback behavior
LRECL padding/truncation and return codes
risks: Assuming ICEGENER and IEBGENER behave identically under every option can hide data changes

utilities.name: IEBCOPY
utilities.behavior: Copies/merges selected PDS/PDSE members and can unload, reload or compress libraries.
required_evidence: Input/output libraries, member selection/rename/replace and aliases
PDS versus PDSE details and whether load modules or source are involved
risks: An unloaded library is not an ordinary CSV/text dataset
Directory/member identity and replacement semantics matter

utilities.name: IEBUPDTE
utilities.behavior: Updates fixed-length records or library members from control statements.
required_evidence: Control cards, member identities, sequence conventions and full before/after inputs
risks: Do not execute updates against the mainframe
Treat source-changing utility steps as behavior requiring explicit local replacement

utilities.name: IEBCOMPR
utilities.behavior: Compares datasets according to utility controls and returns comparison results.
required_evidence: Exact utility release, SYSUT inputs, control statements and expected messages/return codes
risks: A replacement comparison must preserve comparison granularity, ignored data and failure semantics

utilities.name: IEBDG
utilities.behavior: Generates test data using utility control statements.
required_evidence: Field/record generation controls, seeds, counts and dependencies
risks: Generated data does not establish that business-rule branches were tested
Do not run on mainframe; use evidence-grounded local synthetic generation

utilities.name: IKJEFT01
utilities.behavior: Hosts TSO batch commands; the invoked commands and their environment determine actual application behavior.
required_evidence: SYSTSIN/SYSTSPRT, PARM, STEPLIB and nested command/REXX/CLIST members
Db2 DSN subsystem, RUN PROGRAM/PLAN and parameters when present
Exact terminal-monitor variant and return-code/abend propagation
risks: The driver name does not identify the business program
Driver variants and nested commands must not be assumed equivalent

utilities.name: DSNUTILB
utilities.behavior: Invokes Db2 utilities described by SYSIN and subsystem/utility parameters.
required_evidence: Subsystem, utility ID, SYSIN commands, templates and DDs
LOAD/UNLOAD/REORG/RUNSTATS/COPY or other exact utility semantics, options and restart context
risks: Utilities may modify database state and must never be run by read-only discovery
SQLite is a POC target and cannot imply Db2 utility/transaction equivalence

utilities.name: DSNTIAUL
utilities.behavior: IBM sample program that unloads Db2 table/query results to sequential datasets.
required_evidence: SQL, program/plan version, parameters, SYSREC and SYSPUNCH output definitions
Column types, null indicators, encoding and load-control output
risks: A sequential unload contains format conventions not represented by plain CSV alone
Sample programs may be locally modified; collect the actual version

utilities.name: DSNTEP2
utilities.behavior: IBM productivity-aid sample programs execute supplied SQL; individual programs have distinct features and output formats.
required_evidence: Actual sample program/version, plan/bind settings and SQL input
Commit/rollback boundaries, SQLCODE handling, report formatting and effects
risks: Do not equate different drivers or treat SQL input as read-only merely because it is inside a utility
All updates, DDL and procedure calls remain prohibited during discovery

utilities.name: BPXBATCH
utilities.behavior: Starts z/OS UNIX commands, shell scripts or programs; exact invocation and environment define its behavior.
required_evidence: SH/PGM/SHRC/PGMRC mode, PARM/STDPARM, STDIN/OUT/ERR/ENV
Referenced script/program, profiles, working directory, permissions and code page
Exact BPXBATCH/BPXBATSL variant semantics
risks: Shell commands can perform arbitrary side effects; never execute collected source or command text
Parent/environment/return-code behavior differs by mode and variant

utilities.name: DFSRRC00
utilities.behavior: IMS batch region/controller invocation; PARM and the called program identify the requested IMS processing.
required_evidence: Region type, called program, PSB/DBD/ACB and IMS subsystem configuration
DL/I operations, checkpoints/restart, database allocation and return codes
risks: Driver recognition is not an IMS adapter
IMS transactional and hierarchical data semantics require dedicated evidence

utilities.name: DFHCSDUP
utilities.behavior: Reads and changes CICS system definition resource data using batch commands.
required_evidence: SYSIN commands, CSD version, groups/lists, parameters and exits
Resource definitions and the active runtime overrides used by the application
risks: Never run resource modification commands during discovery
Definitions alone do not implement transaction behavior or screens

topics.title: Authoritative source and dependency closure
checks: Record Endevor environment/system/subsystem/type/stage, member/version and export time when available. Do not assume an exported member matches the deployed load module.
Collect COPY/REPLACE, SQL INCLUDE/DCLGEN, PROC/INCLUDE, control cards, macros and dynamic CALL targets. Duplicate names across libraries require resolution.
Preserve original bytes/hash and record export encoding and line-ending conversion. The current intake requires UTF-8 text exports; binary/native records need a reviewed adapter.

topics.title: Dataset structure and character encoding
checks: Record RECFM, LRECL, BLKSIZE, DSORG, CCSID/code page and transfer mode before interpreting offsets. FB/VB/U data is not automatically newline-delimited text.
For variable records, distinguish payload from record/block descriptors. Packed decimals, signed/zoned values and binary fields must not pass through text transcoding.
Preserve significant spaces, low/high values, record padding, alternate encodings and invalid-data behavior.

topics.title: COBOL representation and execution semantics
checks: Resolve compiler dialect/options, fixed format/continuations/debug lines, truncation/rounding/size errors and collating sequence.
Account for every branch and statement, level-88 values, REDEFINES, OCCURS DEPENDING ON, reference modification, edited pictures and decimal scale.
Resolve PERFORM fall-through, INITIAL/CANCEL, working-storage lifetime, dynamic CALL, file status, SORT exits and exception handling; unsupported features remain blocked.

topics.title: Job, step and scheduler execution
checks: Expand PROC/INCLUDE, symbolic parameters and DD overrides with provenance; retain execution order and each call site.
COND tests specify bypass conditions. IF/THEN/ELSE, abends, EVEN/ONLY and skipped-step return codes require explicit modeling; never translate COND by intuition.
Capture calendar/business-date, predecessors, triggers, reruns, restart points and external scheduler events. CA7 or other vendor definitions need application documentation.

Identify DD * and DD DATA boundaries and any DLM setting; JCL-looking text inside in-stream data is not automatically an executing step. Preserve the consuming program and possible downstream effects as separate evidence.

topics.title: Dataset allocation, ownership and generations
checks: Capture DISP normal/abnormal actions, temporary && datasets, PASS, concatenation, GDG generations and catalog aliases.
Capture VSAM organization, primary/alternate keys, duplicate policy, empty-file/EOF behavior, locking, file status and restart positioning.
Platform-specific allocation may be replaced, but its business-visible existence/content/lifecycle must be verified before exemption.

topics.title: Control cards and application utilities
checks: A utility invocation is not a business program and not an automatic exemption. Read every control card and nested command and record its effects.
Resolve product/version, installation defaults, exits and site aliases such as SORT; collect outputs, error handling and return-code changes.
Add local wrapper details in application-knowledge.json. Its text supplies hypotheses/evidence, never an executable adapter or a conversion approval.

topics.title: Db2 to SQLite boundaries
checks: Capture schema/owner, views, keys, constraints, indexes, triggers, routines, CCSIDs, NULL indicators and exact decimal types; catalog visibility is limited by account permissions.
Capture SQLCODE/SQLSTATE, cursors, ordering, isolation/commit/rollback and package/bind options. No explicit ORDER BY means row order is not guaranteed.
SQLite target tests cannot prove Db2 locking, utility, encoding, concurrency or stored-procedure equivalence. Catalog descriptions and sample rows do not prove all runtime constraints.

topics.title: CICS/BMS interaction and transaction boundaries
checks: Map transaction ID to programs/mapsets, screen fields, validation, navigation/PF keys and SEND/RECEIVE flow.
Capture pseudo-conversation, COMMAREA/channels/containers, queues, syncpoints, security and asynchronous work.
Count legacy screens, new React screens and REST endpoints independently with lineage; a generated form does not establish CICS parity.

topics.title: Interfaces and observable effects
checks: Inventory files, Db2, MQ, IMS, CICS, network/FTP, emails, reports and other external boundaries with direction, schedule, format and acknowledgement/error semantics.
Resolve all nested TSO/REXX/CLIST/USS command chains without executing them.
Model retry, deduplication, ordering, partial failure and restart where relevant; side effects unsupported by the target remain unresolved.

topics.title: Rule-driven synthetic evidence
checks: Derive records and relational constraints from legacy source and approved SME interpretation, independently of generated Python.
Include boundary/equality/NULL/blank/invalid/duplicate/missing-match/empty-file cases, interactions and cross-file keys only where those semantics are evidenced.
Identify unreachable or contradictory conditions and budget-limited combinations explicitly; no finite suite demonstrates every possible input. Four seed records are not proof of 85 rules.

topics.title: What evidence can and cannot establish
checks: Track source-line accounting, semantic-unit coverage, extracted-rule tests and business requirements as separate denominators; do not convert an exclusion into a passing test.
An omitted platform operation needs documented rationale, target responsibility and verification. Unsupported or unknown semantics block completion.
Source-derived expected output is an analysis oracle, not observed legacy execution. Mainframe execution and writes are prohibited; do not report measured mainframe parity.
